short: Hierarchical Ti3C2T@MoS2 heterostructures: A first principle
title: Hierarchical Ti3C2T@MoS2 heterostructures: A first principles calculation and application in corrosion/wear protection

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Epoxy coatings on steel need a better corrosion barrier and better wear resistance. A Ti3C2Tx@MoS2 heterostructure, joining two layered lubricants, should improve epoxy corrosion and wear protection.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/method), n7 (DES/modification), n8 (DES/variable_sweep), n9 (PRC/synthesis), n10 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Six MoS2-on-Ti3C2T2 registries I-VI: S or Mo placed above T, C(1) or Ti(1) sites. Interconnected MoS2 nanosheets grow over Ti3C2Tx sheets, forming a hierarchical 2D structure.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Interface binding ranks Ti3C2(OH)2@MoS2 (EB ~ -1.1 eV) >> Ti3C2F2@MoS2 (~0) > Ti3C2O2@MoS2 (unbound, +0.2 to +0.45 eV). Charge redistribution at the OH/MoS2 interface (H gains, S loses charge) adds electrostatic binding absent with O and F terminations.
states.detail: Absorbed: n5 (PRP/value), n6 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n16 (MEC/pathway), n17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Dispersion-corrected DFT (DFT-D); plain GGA cannot bind vdW heterostructures; Negative EB means exothermic assembly and a stable heterostructure; A larger capacitive arc, |Z|0.01Hz and Rc mean better corrosion resistance; A second time constant in the Nyquist plot means the electrolyte has reached the coating/substrate interface; MoS2 (weak interlayer vdW) and Ti3C2Tx (layered, low shear strength) are established solid lubricants

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The 0.1 coating keeps the highest impedance over 9 d in 3.5 wt% NaCl (Rc ~1.1e6 vs EP ~9e4 ohm cm2)
states.detail: Absorbed: n18 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: A larger capacitive arc, |Z|0.01Hz and Rc mean better corrosion resistance

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: OH-terminated Ti3C2Tx binds MoS2 most stably; 0.1 wt% Ti3C2Tx@MoS2 gives epoxy the best corrosion and wear protection

nodes.solves: Charge redistribution at the OH/MoS2 interface (H gains, S loses charge) adds electrostatic binding absent with O and F terminations
nodes.note: no panels offered (tier C); which row is the interface and which atoms carry the lobes cannot be read from the slice

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Ti3C2(OH)2@MoS2: EB -1.09 to -1.13 eV in all six configurations, VI lowest, II highest. Ti3C2O2@MoS2: EB positive in all configurations, +0.22 to +0.45 eV, highest for I and IV.
nodes.solves: Interface binding ranks Ti3C2(OH)2@MoS2 (EB ~ -1.1 eV) >> Ti3C2F2@MoS2 (~0) > Ti3C2O2@MoS2 (unbound, +0.2 to +0.45 eV)
nodes.note: text order VI > I > III > IV > V > II matches bar heights; system name from on-panel title
nodes.detail: o1: Ti3C2(OH)2@MoS2: EB -1.09 to -1.13 eV in all six configurations, VI lowest, II highest; o2: Ti3C2O2@MoS2: EB positive in all configurations, +0.22 to +0.45 eV, highest for I and IV; o3: Ti3C2F2@MoS2: EB -0.04 to -0.05 eV for II, III, V, VI and +0.02 eV for I and IV
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n5 (o1, o2, o3).

nodes.title: ECHEM:EIS, F8, F9
nodes.head: Day-1 Nyquist plots: single arc for -0.1 and -0.3; EP and -0.5 already show a low-frequency tail. Fitted Rc after 1 d: -0.1 ~1.9e6 > -0.3 ~1.45e6 > EP ~7.6e5 ~ -0.5 ~7.1e5 ohm cm2
nodes.solves: Initial barrier resistance of epoxy rises with 0.1 and 0.3 loading, but not with 0.5
nodes.note: arcs do not shrink monotonically: -0.1 day 6 arc (~1.45e6) exceeds days 2, 3, 9; -0.3 day 9 exceeds day 6; -0.5 day 3 exceeds day 1 linked text gives EP Rc 7.66e6 ohm cm2 at 1 d; the plotted EP point is ~7.6e5 (text exponent wrong; as written it would put EP above -0.1)
nodes.detail: o11: Day-1 Nyquist plots: single arc for -0.1 and -0.3; EP and -0.5 already show a low-frequency tail; o12: Fitted Rc after 1 d: -0.1 ~1.9e6 > -0.3 ~1.45e6 > EP ~7.6e5 ~ -0.5 ~7.1e5 ohm cm2
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n14 (o11, o12).

nodes.title: MECH:wear, F10
nodes.head: Wear rate: -0.1 ~0.09 < -0.3 ~0.13 < EP ~0.18 < -0.5 ~0.28 um3/(N um). Wear-track depth: -0.1 ~ -0.3 ~ -28 to -30 um, EP ~ -35 um, -0.5 ~ -45 um and widest
nodes.solves: Wear rate halves at 0.1 loading and rises with further filler, exceeding EP at 0.5
nodes.note: linked text gives EP 0.7 um3/(N um); the bar is ~0.18, which matches the text's own '-0.1 reduced by about 50%' track widths of -0.1, -0.3 and EP look alike (~1.0 mm); text says -0.1 has the smallest width and -0.3 a larger one, which the profile does not show
